name: american chicken alfredo
instructions:
The AMERICAN alfredo — the cream build, as its own dish (the italian butter-parmesan emulsion lives in [[roman-cheese-pasta]] variant B; this is deliberately the other thing). Poached chicken breast + heavy cream + butter + mozzarella + parmesan, BAKED AT 375°F.

1. POACH the chicken breast; slice or shred.
2. Build the cream sauce: HEAVY CREAM + BUTTER, with PARMESAN melted in.
3. Combine the pasta, chicken, and sauce in a baking dish; MOZZARELLA over the top (and more parmesan).
4. GRATIN: BREADCRUMBS + SPRAY OIL over the top.
5. BAKE AT 375°F until bubbling and browned on top.
notes:
=== THE AMERICAN BRANCH — SEPARATE FROM THE ROMAN EMULSION ===

[[roman-cheese-pasta]]'s alfredo variant is the italian original: butter + parmesan + pasta water, no cream. This recipe is the AMERICANIZED build — heavy cream, mozzarella, poached chicken, baked — recorded as its own dish rather than a variant there (the roman file predicted this: 'if an americanized cream build ever earns a place here, it comes in as its own variant' — it earned a whole recipe instead).

=== THE BUILD ===

- POACHED CHICKEN BREAST (poached, not pan-seared).
- HEAVY CREAM + BUTTER as the sauce base.
- MOZZARELLA + PARMESAN as the cheese pair.
- GRATIN FINISH: breadcrumbs + spray oil over the top.
- BAKED AT 375°F.
- SPINACH is a good secondary ingredient.

=== PASTA SHAPES — GNOCCHI IS SECONDARY, IT DOESN'T BAKE WELL ===

PENNE, FETTUCCINE, or RIGATONI are the pasta. GNOCCHI is SECONDARY to them because it doesn't bake well — it DISSOLVES before the cheese is appropriately crispy.

=== LEMON ZEST — CLASHING (TRIED IT) ===

Lemon zest is CLASHING — I didn't like it when I tried it.
